almanac_tool_shovel: A shovel turns untilled ground into plots and digs things out of them. A growing or ripe plant comes out as one seed of its crop and variety, and a weed, a dead plant or Rotten produce is cleared from the plot. It also digs up trees, which leave their tree seed, and digs out burrows. Hard soil takes two uses and more time than soft ground, and a shovel cannot dig very hard soil.
almanac_tool_pickaxe: A pickaxe breaks rocks and very hard soil. A rock becomes soft untilled ground that a shovel can dig; a rock two tiles long takes two uses and twice the time. Very hard soil becomes Infertile soil, which a shovel cannot till.
almanac_tool_axe: An axe or a chainsaw chops a grown tree: the tree drops one Wood and becomes a stump, and any fruit growing on it is lost. The stump grows back into a young tree, which grows up again before it gives fruit. With the {skill} skill, each chop also drops grafts of that tree.
almanac_tool_bucket: A bucket carries water from a Pump, Pumpjack, Well or Tap to plots and trees. Water a plot or a tree to fill its soil up to the top of the plant's happy water level; the rest stays in the bucket.
almanac_vehicles_p1: Vehicles carry more than you can carry and cover ground faster than you walk. The Quad carries goods between buildings. The Tractor pulls a trailer that plants, fertilizes or harvests every plot it drives over, so one drive along a row does the whole row.
almanac_vehicles_p2_a: You buy vehicles and trailers at a
almanac_vehicles_p2_b: , and Deploy takes one out with you driving it. Drive with W, A, S and D. Drive onto the row in front of the hangar door and press Dock to store it again.
almanac_vehicles_p3_a: Driving uses fuel, and a vehicle stops when its tank is empty. A
almanac_vehicles_p3_b: makes fuel from what you put in it, and a vehicle on a route fills its tank at the station's south side.
almanac_vehicles_p4_a: In Vehicle automation you build a route, a list of stops. A vehicle sent out on a route drives itself from stop to stop and loads or unloads at each, so a field can be planted or harvested and the harvest carried to a machine or a store while you do other work. A
almanac_vehicles_p4_b: sends a vehicle out on its route each time its signal turns on, for example when a Harvest sensor sees that the crops are ready.
almanac_water_p1: Every plant uses water from its plot. At first you fill a [bucket](utility:bucket) at the [Pump](water:pumpjack) and pour it on each plot yourself.
almanac_water_p2: [Pipe](water:pipe) connects Pumps, [Wells](water:well), [Taps](water:tap), [Sprinklers](water:sprinkler) and [Pot stills](machines:still) into one water network. A Tap next to your field fills your bucket there, so you walk to the Pump less often. A Sprinkler waters every growing plot in its area while you do other work.
almanac_water_p3: Every litre taken from a Pump is paid as Water at the [end of the day](concepts:day), at a higher price on Dry and Drought days than on other days. Water from a Well is not paid for, but a Well refills more slowly than a Pump.
almanac_water_p4: A [Valve](water:valve) closes one pipe, so you choose which part of the water network gets water.
almanac_desc_pump: A Pump holds up to {cap} L of water and refills by {rate} L a day. Fill a [bucket](utility:bucket) from it, or connect [pipe](water:pipe) to any of its corners so its water reaches [Taps](water:tap) and [Sprinklers](water:sprinkler). Every litre taken from it is paid as Water at the [end of the day](concepts:day), at a higher price on Dry and Drought days than on other days.
almanac_desc_well: A Well holds up to {cap} L of water, more than a [Pump](water:pumpjack), and refills by {rate} L a day, less than a Pump. Water from a Well is not paid for. On a Drought day it refills {drought}% slower than on other days. Fill a [bucket](utility:bucket) from it, or connect [pipe](water:pipe) to any of its corners.
almanac_desc_tap: A Tap fills a [bucket](utility:bucket) at {rate} L a second from the water network its [pipe](water:pipe) connects it to. Place it next to your field and fill your bucket there instead of at the [Pump](water:pumpjack). A Tap holds no water itself: when the network's Pumps and [Wells](water:well) are empty, it fills only as fast as they refill.
almanac_desc_pipe: Pipe is placed on the edge between two tiles. Connected pipes, and every [Pump](water:pumpjack), [Well](water:well), [Tap](water:tap), [Sprinkler](water:sprinkler) and [Pot still](machines:still) that a pipe touches at a corner, make one water network: water from its Pumps and Wells reaches every building on it. Drag while placing to lay a whole run of pipe at once.
almanac_desc_valve: A Valve is placed on one [pipe](water:pipe); placed where there is no pipe, it lays the pipe as well. Click it and the gardener walks to it and closes or opens it. A closed Valve stops water in its own pipe only: water still reaches the rest of the network through any other open pipe.
almanac_desc_sprinklers: A sprinkler is placed on a corner where four tiles meet. It waters every growing plot and tree in its area, {day} L a day per tile, while [pipe](water:pipe) connects it to a [Pump](water:pumpjack) or [Well](water:well) that holds water. It does not water ripe or empty plots. A Sprinkler waters a {w1}×{h1} area, a Vertical sprinkler a {w2}×{h2} strip that you rotate while placing, and a Large sprinkler a {w3}×{h3} area.
almanac_desc_fertilizer: A {n} L bag from the Additive store. Fertilize a plot or a tree to fill its fertilizer to full, using only the litres the soil is missing. A [Sprayer](vehicles:overview) behind a Tractor fertilizes every plot and tree the Tractor drives over.
almanac_desc_compost: A {liters} L bag that the [Compost box](machines:compost-box) makes from farm waste. It fertilizes a plot or a tree the same as a [Fertilizer bag](utility:fertilizer), and you make it on the farm instead of buying it. A [Sprayer](vehicles:overview) behind a Tractor spreads it over every plot and tree the Tractor drives over.
almanac_desc_weed_spray: A {n} L bag. Spray a tilled plot to remove its [weed](misc:weed); afterwards no weed grows on that plot for longer than after digging or pulling a weed. Buy it at the Additive store, or make it from [Rotten produce](misc:rotten) in a [Pot still](machines:still). A [Sprayer](vehicles:overview) behind a Tractor sprays every plot the Tractor drives over that has a weed or can grow one.
almanac_desc_extract: A {liters} L bag made by crushing [Cut grass](misc:grass) in a [Mill](machines:mill). Pour {pour} L on a growing plant, a sapling or a stump and it grows faster for {seconds}s. On a grown tree out of season it raises the chance that a new season starts. A plant takes Extract once. Infused Extract, made at an [Infuser](machines:infuser), makes a plant grow faster for {infused}s instead, and after the harvest no [weed](misc:weed) grows on its plot for as long as on a plot a weed was dug out of.
almanac_desc_sugar: A {bag} L bag of sugar. The [Jam machine](machines:jam) uses it to make jam. Buy it at the Additive store, or crush [Sugar cane](fruits:sugar-cane) in a [Mill](machines:mill), which costs less per litre than buying it. Sugar does not lose [freshness](concepts:freshness), and the [Market](concepts:market) buys it.
almanac_in_watch: It has no input. It watches the eight tiles around it; placed on a Wooden fence, it watches the whole area that fence closes instead, and stays off while the fence is open.
almanac_in_lever: Each time its input turns on, the lever flips, as if a gardener had flipped it.
almanac_out_lever: On while the lever is up, off while it is down.
almanac_in_button: It has no input; a gardener presses it.
almanac_out_button: On for a short moment after each press, then off.
almanac_in_lamp: It lights while its input is on.
almanac_in_logic: Two inputs, one on its left side and one on its right.
almanac_out_logic: Tuned to OR: on while either input is on. Tuned to AND: on only while both inputs are on.
almanac_out_not: On while the input is off, off while the input is on.
almanac_in_pulser: One input. Only the moment it turns from off to on matters.
almanac_out_pulser: On for a moment when the input turns on, then off until the input turns off and on again.
almanac_in_counter: Adds one to the count for every moment the input is on. From a Pulser, that is one count each time the signal turns on; a signal that stays on counts up many times a second.
almanac_out_counter: On for a moment each time the count reaches Count to, which you set in its panel, up to {max}; the count then starts again from zero. {reset} sets the count back to zero at any time.
almanac_out_water: On while at least one watched plant or tree is wilting, if Wilting is ticked, or drowning, if Overwatered is ticked. Both are ticked when you place it; with neither ticked it stays off.
almanac_out_fert: On while at least one watched growing plant or tree is starving for fertilizer. It has nothing to set.
almanac_out_harvest: Any: on while at least one watched plant is ripe. All: on while every watched plant is ripe, and there is at least one. Trees do not count. It is set to Any when you place it.
almanac_out_variety: On while at least one watched growing or ripe plant, or tree that is not a stump, is Plain, Named or Heirloom, for each one you tick. Plain is ticked when you place it; with none ticked it stays off.
almanac_out_weather: On all day while today's weather is one you tick: Clear, Rain, Dry, Flood or Drought. Clear is ticked when you place it.
almanac_out_day: On while the part of the day is one you tick: Sunrise, Day, Sunset or Twilight. Day is the part the clock at the top calls Midday. Day is ticked when you place it.
almanac_in_pressure: It has no input. It watches its own tile and the eight around it; placed on a Wooden fence, it watches the whole area that fence closes instead, and stays off while the fence is open.
almanac_out_pressure: On while something you tick is on a watched tile. Vehicle: a Quad or Tractor out on the field. You: a gardener. On the ground: an item lying there. Vehicle is ticked when you place it; with none ticked it stays off.
almanac_neighbour_plant: It grows only while another {crop} that is not Heirloom is growing within {reach} tiles of it and is not wilting, drowning or starving for fertilizer.
almanac_neighbour_tree: It gives fruit only while another grown {crop} tree that is not Heirloom is within {reach} tiles of it.
almanac_best_produce: Sold as fruit, it sells for {on}× the price of a Plain {crop}. Made into anything else, it sells for {off}×.
almanac_best_processed: Made into jam or crushed in the Mill, it sells for {on}× the price of a Plain {crop}. Sold as fruit or made into alcohol, it sells for {off}×.
almanac_best_alcohol: Made into alcohol in the Pot still or a Barrel, it sells for {on}× the price of a Plain {crop}. Sold as fruit or preserved, it sells for {off}×.
almanac_study_hint: Study this fruit at the Crop Variety Station {n} more times
almanac_study_hint_once: Study this fruit at the Crop Variety Station once more
almanac_tree_seasons: A grown tree gives fruit in seasons of {days} days, and gives fruit more slowly between seasons. A happy tree gives fruit faster and starts its next season sooner. The fruit drops on the ground around the tree; pick it up before it loses freshness.

almanac_rarity_p1_b: is a skill, not a fifth grade.
almanac_rarity_p2: Uncommon, Rare, and Heirloom fruit show a small colored mark: green, blue, or gold. Common fruit has none.

almanac_rarity_p7: Seed you shovel off a plant keeps that plant's grade. Fruit that drops from a tree has its own grade — most Common, some Uncommon, few Rare, almost never Heirloom. The tree itself has no grade.

almanac_research_p1: Research is your husband's work so the farm can grow past the starter tools and crops. Open Research from the same buttons as Shop and the Build menu to pick a job.
almanac_research_p2: He can run only one job at a time. Starting a job spends money up front. The job takes time in seconds while you garden. When it finishes, new things appear in the shop and the Build menu, and you can buy more land.
almanac_research_p3_a: Research is how you get new crops, tools, water,
almanac_research_p3_c: are not research — spend those on
almanac_variety_p1: Variety is what the plant is. Potato and Bintje are two Varieties of potato — siblings, not steps. Each Variety is good for one of three things: Fresh, the fruit sold as it is; Preserving, the Jam machine and the Mill; or Alcohol, the Pot still and the Barrel. The Market pays more for a Variety used the way it is meant, and less for one used any other way. The plain crop is even at all three. A seed pack tells you what its Variety is best for before you plant it.
almanac_quality_p1: Quality is how well the plant was treated, shown as a percent. The Market pays more for higher Quality fruit of the same Variety. A seed you shovel keeps that plant's Quality, and a stack of the same Variety averages Quality. Seed you buy starts at 0%. Happiness while the plant grows is the live care; Quality is set when the fruit ripens. Tree fruit is 0%.
almanac_variety_desc_carrot: A sweet orange root. Sold as it is.
almanac_variety_desc_potato: An all-purpose tuber. Eaten as it is, or distilled.
almanac_variety_desc_wheat: A bread wheat. Flour, and beer.
almanac_variety_desc_tomato: A round red tomato. Ketchup, and the table.
almanac_variety_desc_raspberry: A red raspberry. Eaten as it is, or jammed.
almanac_variety_desc_grape: A wine-and-table grape. Jelly, and wine.
almanac_variety_desc_vanilla: A vanilla orchid. Crushed for extract.
almanac_variety_desc_sugar_cane: A chewing cane. Crushed for sugar.
almanac_variety_desc_apple: A dual-purpose apple. Eaten as it is, or pressed for cider.
almanac_variety_desc_apricot: A dual-purpose apricot. Table, jam, and brandy.
almanac_variety_desc_olive: A dual-purpose olive. Table, or crushed for oil.
almanac_variety_desc_cherry: A sweet-and-pie cherry. Eaten as it is, or jammed.
almanac_variety_desc_bintje: A Dutch potato grown for frying and for spirit.
almanac_variety_desc_russian_banana: A yellow fingerling, buttery when eaten as it is.
almanac_variety_desc_sonora: A hard white wheat from Sonora. Distills well.
almanac_variety_desc_red_fife: A Canadian wheat. Makes strong flour.
almanac_variety_desc_green_zebra: A tart green-striped tomato, eaten as it is.
almanac_variety_desc_san_marzano: An Italian plum tomato grown for sauce.
almanac_variety_desc_black_raspberry: A wild American raspberry grown for jam.
almanac_variety_desc_concord: An American grape grown for jelly.
almanac_variety_desc_thompson: A seedless table grape, eaten as it is.
almanac_variety_desc_keknyelu: A Hungarian wine grape from Badacsony. Needs another grape nearby that is not Heirloom.
almanac_variety_desc_pink_lady: A crisp eating apple. Needs another apple tree nearby that is not Heirloom.
almanac_variety_desc_moorpark: A large apricot, eaten as it is.
almanac_variety_desc_klosterneuburger: An Austrian apricot grown for brandy.
almanac_variety_desc_blenheim: A Royal Blenheim apricot, grown for jam.
almanac_variety_desc_kalamata: A Greek table olive, eaten as it is.
almanac_variety_desc_arbequina: A Spanish olive grown for oil.
almanac_variety_desc_montmorency: A tart pie cherry, grown for jam.
almanac_variety_desc_bing: A sweet eating cherry. Needs another cherry tree nearby that is not Heirloom.
almanac_mushrooms_p1: Fly agaric and Truffle are mushrooms that come up around grown trees. At the end of each day, each grown tree can put one mushroom on an untilled tile where its fruit lands. Plots and paving never get one, so leave some ground untilled around a tree if you want mushrooms.
almanac_mushrooms_p2: Each grown tree's chance of a mushroom, by the weather of the day that just ended, for a tree at half happiness. The second number is what each rank of {skill} adds to that chance:
almanac_mushrooms_happy: A happier tree gets mushrooms more often. At full happiness a tree's chance is {max} times the chance above, and with no happiness it is {min} times.
almanac_mushrooms_p3: The share of Truffles among a tree's mushrooms, by the tree's Variety:
almanac_mushrooms_p4: A mushroom stays for {days} days, then it is gone. Pick it up with an empty hand, or onto a stack of the same mushroom.
almanac_mushrooms_p5: Crush a Truffle at a Mill into {n} Truffle extract. Truffle extract and Fly agaric infuse goods at an Infuser, and both mushrooms go into the Compost box and the Furnace. Fly agaric also turns up in Uncommon burrows, and Truffle in Rare ones.
almanac_burrow_p1: A burrow is a hole in untilled ground. Dig it with a shovel and one item drops next to it. Nothing shows what you will get until you dig. Digging a burrow does not till the ground, and a pickaxe does nothing to it. You can walk across a burrow, but you cannot place, pave, fence, or plant a tree on it. A Treasure adds its money when you pick it up.
almanac_burrow_p2: {start} burrows are on the farm when you start. Overnight, each piece of land you own can get one new burrow on untilled ground. A burrow stays until you dig it.
almanac_burrow_p3: What you dig up is Common, Uncommon, or Rare, chosen when you dig. The farther the burrow is from the house door, and the later in the game you dig it, the more often you get an Uncommon or Rare item. Each dig that does not give a Rare item raises the chance of Rare on your next dig by {step}%. Digging up a Rare item sets that extra chance back to zero.
almanac_infusion_p1: Infusion is adding one item to a good at the Infuser. Each good takes one of two items, listed below. The good keeps its name, its Quality, and the money the Market pays for it, and shows a plus. Infused goods sell at Market at the percent shown for that good. Selling them does not change that percent. Finishing a contract with Infused goods raises Reputation more than the same contract without them. Infused Extract makes a plant grow faster for longer than Extract does, and the Market does not buy it.
almanac_infusion_p2: Flakes come from crushing Chilli at a Mill, Vanilla extract from crushing Vanilla, and Truffle extract from crushing a Truffle. Fly agaric comes up around trees.
